records.title: [CS-065-1] Implement GET /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/documents/tree endpoint with recursive query
records.body:
## Objective

- Implement GET /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/documents/tree endpoint with recursive query

---

## Task Boundary Guidance

- Prefer **one primary execution surface** and **one dominant specialization** per task (e.g., API endpoint, UI view, worker job, integration test).
- Avoid mixing backend behavior + frontend UI + audit/telemetry in one task unless the change is tiny and inseparable.
- If a task must include a side effect (audit log, event emission), make it explicit in the objective and validation.
- This task has one primary execution surface: api.
- Avoid coupling UI and backend side effects in this task.
- If side effects expand materially, split into a dedicated follow-up task.

---

## Deliverables

- Tree endpoint returns nested folders/documents per API contract.
- Workspace scoping enforced with NOT_WORKSPACE_MEMBER.

---

## Files

| Path | Change Type | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| apps/api/src/modules/documents/documents.controller.ts | add | api | Document tree endpoint contract. |
| apps/api/src/modules/documents/documents.service.ts | add | api | Recursive tree query and assembly logic. |
| apps/api/src/modules/documents/dto/documents-tree.query.dto.ts | add | api | Tree query DTO; filename may vary. |

---

## Spec References

- docs/agent-ref/api/document-endpoints.md
- docs/agent-ref/rules/workspace-isolation.md
- docs/spec/05-features/05.4-documents.md
- docs/spec/12-errors/12.4-error-code-catalog.md

---

## Implementation Notes

- Endpoint: GET /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/documents/tree.
- Error codes: NOT_WORKSPACE_MEMBER, WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND.
- Domain events: none (read-only endpoint).

---

## Constraints

- Workspace isolation: all workspace-owned queries must include workspace_id.
- REST must not return collaborative Yjs content.
- Follow response envelope and canonical error codes.
- Follow AGENTS and docs/agent-ref contracts.
- Follow module AGENTS and `docs/agent-ref` contracts.

---

## Validation

Commands:
```bash
pnpm -w lint
pnpm -w test
API_BASE_URL="${API_BASE_URL:-http://localhost:3001}"
curl -fsS "$API_BASE_URL/api/v1/health"
```
Expected outcomes:
- Positive path: nested tree returned with folders and documents ordered by position.
- Negative path: NOT_WORKSPACE_MEMBER for non-member access.
- If not run, explain why and risk.

---

## Done When

- [ ] Deliverables implemented.
- [ ] Validation commands executed or explicitly waived.
- [ ] Errors/envelopes match docs/agent-ref.
- [ ] No scope creep beyond listed files.
- [ ] Handoff completed.

---

## Handoff

- Summary of changes:
- Validation evidence:
- Open issues / follow-ups:
- Risks or deviations:

---

- AGENTS.md
- docs/agent-ref/*

records.title: [RCRD-07] Corrections: preserve original, link replacement, impact analysis
records.body:
> **Blocked by:** #168, #165 · **Blocks:** `INTL-08` (pending)
>
> _dependency graph — auto-rendered from the ticket frontmatter (issue #52)_

# RCRD-07 — Corrections: preserve original, link replacement, impact analysis

Implements PRD §12.3 — requirement **COR-002**, epic `E24-RECORDS`.
No ADR — the decision is already made in PRD §12.3 (*"Confirmed errors MUST create a Correction,
preserve the original answer, create or link a replacement Answer Snapshot, run impact analysis and
notify affected customers when required"*) and PRD §35.8 invariants 5 and 6; this is build ticket 7 of
9 against it.
Parent sub-PRD: [17-records-collab README](../README.md). Master spec: [PRD](../../../PRD.md).
Depends on: [RCRD-06 — Issue reports at answer/claim/citation/source level](RCRD-06-issue-reports-at-answer-claim-citation-source-level.md)
· [RCRD-03 — Record↔answer linkage, rerun under current law, version diff](RCRD-03-record-answer-linkage-rerun-under-current-law-version-diff.md)
**Why `builder`:** a bounded change inside one module's declared file-scope against a fixed contract —
PRD §12.3 fixes the four obligations and `RCRD-03`/`RCRD-06` supply the replacement and the trigger;
this composes them.

## Background + basis

**PRD §12.3 User issues and corrections**, the whole basis:

> Users MUST be able to report incorrect citations, outdated sources, wrong jurisdiction/date,
> unsupported claims, missing authority and privacy issues at answer/claim/citation/source level.
> **Confirmed errors MUST create a Correction, preserve the original answer, create or link a
> replacement Answer Snapshot, run impact analysis and notify affected customers when required.**

Four obligations in one sentence: **create**, **preserve**, **link**, **analyse-and-notify**. Each is
a deliverable below.

**Requirement COR-002** (PRD §30.2): *"Confirmed correction preserves original, links replacement and
performs impact analysis | **Internal issue flow** | correction endpoints | App | **Affected records
become reviewable/notifyable**."* The primary surface is the internal issue flow — sub-PRD **D9**.

**PRD §35.8**, the two invariants that make this mechanical rather than aspirational:

> 5. Formal snapshots and legal corpus versions have **no UPDATE/DELETE application path**;
>    corrections **append replacements**.
> 6. Outbox event and corresponding business state commit **in one transaction**.

**PRD §35.6**, the storage contract:

> | `issue_report` / `correction` | tenant target/category/description/status; **replacement and
> impact linkage** | **original answer preserved** |

**PRD §34.5** carries the customer-visible marker: the Answer Snapshot payload includes
`"correction_state": "NONE"`. That field is how `RCRD-08`'s correction badge and `19-exports`'
correction banner are driven (sub-PRD **D12**, **QR-3**), and `UAT-EXP-01` depends on it:
*"Export old corrected answer → Export shows original legal date/release and **correction banner**; no
regeneration."*

**PRD §32.6** requires a **correction badge** in the Research Record header, and gives the transition
that impact analysis performs:

> | Any active state | `REVIEW_REQUIRED` | system/admin/reviewer | **correction**, source change or
> material issue; **reason required** |
> | `REVIEW_REQUIRED` | `IN_REVIEW` | owner/reviewer | **replacement/rerun linked** |

**PRD §33.4 steps 7–9** give the shape impact analysis must follow — written there for the
source-change path (`16-monitor-alerts`/`WTCH-03`), and the same shape applies here:

> 7. Transaction creates tenant alerts and **marks materially affected records `REVIEW_REQUIRED`**.
> 8. **Outbox delivers** in-app/email/webhook **idempotently**.
> 9. Customer can rerun; **the original answer remains unchanged**.

**PRD §8.11 / §16.2**: internal administration covers *"issue triage and corrections"* and MUST be
*"separated under `/internal/v1`, require internal identity, MFA and short sessions"*. Sub-PRD **D9**
therefore mounts this area's **create/confirm** operation behind `RUNT-02`'s `internal` admission
profile as a per-route override, while reads stay `tenant`. `22-internal-admin`/`INTL-08` is
`blocked_by` this ticket and builds the console on top (plan §5.23).

**PRD §39.5**: the impact-analysis worker belongs to the `maintenance` queue class — *"cleanup,
**impact matching**, usage reconciliation"*, priority 4, cooperative and bounded. That is the same
class `WTCH-02`'s change matcher uses, and it is the reason impact analysis is a job rather than a
synchronous request: PRD §13.2 gives no latency objective for it, and an unbounded fan-out inside an
HTTP request would violate §38.5's request-size and concurrency discipline.

**PRD §42.7** lists `docs/runbooks/legal-correction.md` as required *"before generated answers"*. That
file is `18-ops-release`/`RLSE-10`'s; this ticket provides the mechanism the runbook describes and must
not write `docs/runbooks/**`.

**Accepted caveats carried forward, documented not enforced here:**

- **`correction` is a `DATA-07` table and this ticket has no `blocked_by DATA-07` edge**
  (sub-PRD **QR-1**), exactly as for `RCRD-06`. In the global schedule `01-app-data` delivers roughly
  twelve waves earlier. **If the repository is absent, stop and write back** to
  `docs/prd/breakdown-plan.md` §5.18 + §6.2 and this module's README; never create the table here
  (plan **A3**, **R4**).
- **This ticket has no `blocked_by FND-08` and no `blocked_by RCRD-04` edge** (sub-PRD **QR-2**), yet
  it must move affected records to `REVIEW_REQUIRED`. It therefore writes the transition through
  **`DATA-06.applyReviewAction(tx, ctx, { recordId, fromStatus, toStatus: 'REVIEW_REQUIRED',
  actorId: system, reason })`** — the structural half of PRD §35.8 invariant 7, reachable through
  `RCRD-01 → DATA-06`. `DATA-06` states the split explicitly: *"There is no other write path to
  `workflow_status` … **Which transitions are *legal* is `RCRD-04`'s (via `FND-08`)**."* If the
  Builder finds it

records.title: Feature: Visual drag-and-drop role hierarchy for tiered permissions
records.body:
## Summary
Add a vtiger-style role hierarchy builder so admins can visually model organizational authority and use that hierarchy for tiered permissions.

This should be more than a flat roles table. Roles need a parent/child structure where higher roles can be granted access to users, records, and administrative scope beneath them, while sibling branches remain isolated unless sharing rules explicitly open them.

## Reference Example
The live database example attached to the original request shows a tree like:

```text
Organization
├── ADMIN/EXEC
└── Exec
    ├── Sales Ops
    └── Operations Total
        ├── Partner Admin TEMPLATE
        ├── MobileSage
        └── Exagrow
```

The important behavior is the tree relationship: `Operations Total` sits below `Exec`, while `Partner Admin TEMPLATE`, `MobileSage`, and `Exagrow` sit beneath `Operations Total`. This enables permissions to be reasoned about by branch instead of by unrelated role names.

## User Story
As an Omnir administrator, I need to create and rearrange roles in a visual hierarchy so the CRM can enforce tiered permissions that match the real organization.

## Functional Requirements
- Provide an admin UI for roles as a hierarchical tree, similar to vtiger's role editor.
- Show a clear root node, such as `Organization`, with nested role nodes underneath.
- Support drag-and-drop reparenting of roles onto another role or back to the root level.
- Support sibling ordering so admins can keep the tree readable.
- Support create, rename, archive/delete, and move actions from the hierarchy view.
- Provide expand/collapse for branches and enough indentation/connector styling to make ancestry obvious.
- Prevent invalid moves, including cycles, moving a role beneath itself, cross-tenant moves, or orphaning required system roles.
- Warn or require confirmation before moves that change access for users or records under that branch.
- Persist moves transactionally and handle optimistic UI rollback if the API rejects the move.

## Permissions Semantics
- Role hierarchy should be available to the authorization layer, not just stored for display.
- Users assigned to a role are considered part of that role's branch.
- A higher role should be able to receive configurable visibility/admin authority over descendant roles.
- Descendant roles should not automatically gain access upward.
- Sibling branches should not automatically see each other.
- Module/action permissions still apply; hierarchy should determine scope, not bypass object-level privileges.
- Sharing rules should be able to override or extend hierarchy visibility where needed.

## Backend / Data Model Notes
- Roles should be tenant-scoped.
- Store parent relationship and sibling order, e.g. `parent_role_id` plus `sort_order`.
- Consider a materialized path, closure table, or equivalent helper structure if descendant lookups become hot in permission checks.
- API should expose endpoints for reading the full hierarchy, creating roles, updating role metadata, and moving/reordering roles.
- Move operations should validate cycle prevention server-side, even if the UI also blocks invalid drops.
- Changes should be audit logged because hierarchy edits can materially alter access.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Admin can view the role hierarchy as a visual tree.
- Admin can drag a role under another role and see the new parent/child relationship persist after refresh.
- Admin can reorder sibling roles and see order persist after refresh.
- Invalid drag targets are visibly rejected and cannot be saved.
- Moving a role updates permission-scope calculations for affected users.
- Existing flat role permissions continue to work after hierarchy is introduced.
- Role hierarchy is isolated per organization/tenant.
- Automated tests cover hierarchy move validation, cycle prevention, descendant lookup, and permission-scope behavior.

## Open Questions
- Should hierarchy grant view-only descendant access by default, or should each module/action explicitly opt into descendant visibility?
- Do we need separate concepts for reporting hierarchy vs. administrative hierarchy, or can one tree serve both for the first implementation?
- Which roles should be protected system roles that cannot be deleted or moved?

records.title: What I'd Build Next
records.body:
A running list of what would come next if BlockWorks were a production SDK — in rough priority order.

## Roadmap Items

- **DataFusion engine** — DataFusion is the next engine to slot in via the same sidecar-store + `prefix:*` dispatch pattern that the Polars integration uses. Parquet is the on-disk frame format. The runtime sees no difference; only the block author's import changes.

- **Block marketplace** — versioned manifests, dependency resolution between blocks whose output schemas feed each other. Extends the manifest format, adds a registry server, keeps the runtime unchanged.

- **Schema evolution** — when upstream output changes, downstream blocks need migration paths. Automatic compatibility checks with clear error messages rather than silent breakage.

- **Capability system** — `ctx.http`, `ctx.fs`, `ctx.llm` as registered capabilities rather than methods on `EngineAPI`. The `BlockContext` already reads this way; the change is moving from a fixed `engine` field to a `capabilities` map.

- **Execution sandboxing** — AI-generated blocks currently run in the main process via `new Function`. A Node `vm` context or Web Worker with a capability allow-list would let community blocks run without trusting their code.

- **Column arithmetic** — `engine.addComputedColumn(frameId, expression)` lets blocks derive new columns (e.g. `revenue = quantity * price`) without pushing a full pipeline of custom transforms.

- **Streaming execution** — row-batch streaming through the pipeline for files larger than memory. Requires changing `FrameStore` from full-frame IDs to batched iterators; the block author's API stays the same.

- **Telemetry overlay** — per-node timing and row counts rendered on the canvas, plus a "slow node" hint system.

---

Discussion welcome — open a comment or a separate issue for any of these.

records.title: US-2.5: Data Lineage & Impact Analysis for Quality Issues
records.body:
## User Story

- **As a:** Data Steward
- **I want:** to visualize data lineage and identify downstream systems affected by a quality issue
- **So that:** I can quickly assess impact and notify affected teams

## Acceptance Criteria
- Visual graph showing data flow from source to destination
- Highlights contaminated data path when issue is detected
- Shows all downstream consumers of affected data
- Provides impact report (# of records, systems, dashboards affected)
- Supports automated notifications to affected team owners
- Enables tracing back to root cause (which source or transformation caused issue)

## Implementation Notes
- Build DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) of data pipelines
- Integrate with metadata repository (Apache Atlas or Collibra)
- Use graph database for fast traversal

---
**Epic:** EPIC 2  
**Status:** Not Started  
**Type:** User Story
